title: Cross-Model Sycophancy Contagion in Multi-Agent Debate

original_idea.body: Cross-Model Sycophancy Contagion. Problem: no benchmark for model-to-model sycophancy: does an open model abandon a correct answer when a peer agent confidently disagrees? Direction: pair two open models in a debate over verifiable questions, one correct one confidently wrong, measure flip rate and whether confident-wrong is more contagious than tentative-wrong.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: model-to-model sycophancy contagion is a concrete medium-horizon multi-agent risk labs underweight.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two-model debate scripting on verifiable questions.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused contagion-rate metric; orchestration adds modest scope.

low_compute.reasoning: Two small models in dialogue, single GPU/API.

novelty.reasoning: Model-to-model contagion in debate is plausibly mostly novel vs user-directed sycophancy.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Model-to-model sycophancy contagion in debate appears under-explored vs user-directed sycophancy.
